body: Poor trip. Seen some rabid monkeys. Shown around a cinnamon farm and a herb garden where upselling was rhe game and they both asked for tips . Was told id see crocodiles etc. At the end was left to walk back up a dark road to find transport back to Mirrissa. Stay clear!
title: Keep a wide berth.

body: Koggala Lake is an absolute paradise for nature lovers and anyone looking for a peaceful escape. The lake’s serene waters, surrounded by lush greenery, create a breathtakingly beautiful and tranquil atmosphere. Taking a boat ride across the lake was the perfect way to explore its hidden gems.One of the highlights was visiting the cinnamon farm, where I got to see how authentic Sri Lankan cinnamon is grown and processed. The aroma of fresh cinnamon filled the air, and the locals were incredibly welcoming, happily sharing their knowledge and offering a taste of their products.Another unforgettable stop was the small Buddhist temple on one of the islands. The peaceful surroundings and spiritual energy made it a truly special place.Our Tuk-Tuk driver Mali was very happy to share insights into the temple’s history and teachings.Beyond the scenic beauty, what stood out the most was the warmth of the local people. Everyone I met was friendly and hospitable, making the experience even more memorable.Koggala Lake is a must-visit if you’re in Sri Lanka. Whether you’re interested in nature, culture, or just a relaxing boat ride, this place offers a perfect blend of beauty and authenticity.
title: One place to visit

body: Considering all the previous reviews, they are probably all correct, depending upon prior expectations and actual experience.Prices are negotiable. Go to the tuktuk and tourist information point. Ask how much, offer less. We paid around 40 GBP for two, and small tip. Mangrove fringed lake, some bird life, some grey langur monkeys unless they have got stuffed with free issue bananas. Some fish. Didn’t see crocodiles.Cinnamon island was nice - some learning and a demonstration of bark peeling. All in all, just over an hour, it’s a big stretch to make it to two hours.
title: A pleasant little outing

body: We had a boat trip in this wonderful lake . We visited an old temple in an island inside the lake, and we did a foot fish therapy in another island . Highly recommended
title: Nice lake

body: Very poor value. Overpriced and had a lousy guide. He was very well meaning but did not know much about what was going on. The boat kept stalling and we fell well short of the allotted time. Certainly not something we would repeat and ended up being the most disappointing activity on our holiday.
title: one to avoid….

body: Pleasant environment bordered by mangroves allowing you to take pretty photos but quite disappointed because the wildlife announced was not there apart from a few monkeys, cormorants and egrets.For those who don't know, disembark on one of the islands where we are offered tea while a person briefly explains to us the work to obtain cinnamon sticks.Expensive service: 10,000 RS for 2 so don’t hesitate to negotiate
title: Expensive service

body: 🏄‍♂️🚣‍♂️🤽‍♂️THE WORLD IS A BOOK AND THOSE WHO DO NOT TRAVEL READ ONLY ONE PAGE🏄‍♀️🚣‍♀️🤽‍♀️****
title: Amazing experience

body: We all really enjoyed this. Saw lots of birds and friendly wild monkeys. Visited Cinnamon Island and saw their artisan production.
title: Birds, monkeys and cinnamon

body: Island is good. But never buy cinnamon powder from there. It is a full cheating business. Saw dust is given.
title: Do not buy cinnamon from cinnamon island

body: Totally disagree with all negative reviews. Arrived by tuk tuk and negotiated a cheap price for the boat. Within a few minutes we saw loads of black monkeys, we saw two crocodiles, two huge water lizards, loads of birds. On the way back our guide spotted monkeys, he slowly got the boat to the trees and we were so fortunate to be able to feed them bananas which they took from our hands. The mother was watching which was a bit scary but all part of the experience. Cinnamon Island was really interesting, the man has lived there all of his life making small amounts of money from cinnamon. No pressure at all to buy anything. The fish spa was brilliant and such a great experience. Yes we were fortunate to see what we did but I would not be put off by negative reviews. For info we got the boat around 11am and we saw loads.
title: Great experience

body: Our tuktuk driver brought us to this lake. At the boat company we saw nice pictures of the wildlife: various bird species, crocodiles, monkeys, varanes, ... Also a trip to cinnamon island and fish foot eating/massage was on the list.What we got was 1 monkey in a tree right after departure, no other wildlife, a long and slow ride in the lake with nothing to see. And when the wind was behind us we also could smell the fumes from the engine. The cinamon island experience was just about sniffing at some crushed leaves and being invited for the tea at the home of some people living there, the fish foot massage was not included in the price.Apparently it was a chance in a hundred you will see a crocodile here as there are only 3 or 4. And for special birds you might have had a chance if you would come very early in the morning.So we felt cheated: our expectations were not managed at all, the boat guide was just reacting positively on our enthousiasm. If we would have been informed that we didn´t have a serious chance of seeing wildlife and what the cinnamon island experience was about, we would not have taken this boat trip. And possibly have given a 3 or 4 dot reaction because of their honesty. In stead we like to give this the lowest score as an advice to others.
title: Misleading info

body: Could be a lovely experience as the lake is beautiful with Eagles soaring above, monkeys etc. However it is as other reviewer T bar has said tourist trap after tourist trap.
title: Visit to Koggala Lake

body: Had two trips out onto Koggala Lake recently, one via a local boat owning family and one via Kola Cafe. Lake is very peaceful and Temple Island well worth a visit. We left out Cinnamon Island and fish foot massage. We saw monkeys and fruit bats, but surprisingly few birds, compared to other similar places we've visited over the years. When arranging a price, be clear as to how long you want to go for and where you want to visit, as this will prevent confusion. Best times of day - morning from around 0900 and late afternoon.
title: Very peaceful

body: Do not waste your time or money, much better things to do around here then this. It's a tourist trap filled with tourists traps. Basically you pay to be brought to one tourist trap after the other.
title: Not worth your time or money

body: It was great to visit koggala lake. We went the place could Ananda spice. It costs 3000 fo 5 of us. 1 our and 30 minutes. Beautiful..
Cosmetic and oils not natural there. And expensive, comparing with other marckets. I wouldn’t recommend anybody such bad quality.
title: No recommend

body: This is one of the largest lakes in Southern Sri Lanka. Number of islands are scattered in the lake among which Madol Duwa and Thalathu Duwa are famous. The lake is rich in birdlife and mangroves and is a major tourist attraction for tourists. My visit to Koggala started from Koggala Lake. Mr. Nishantha who works at our staff is from Habaraduwa. He has pre-arranged the visit to Koggala Lake with one of his friends. Early morning we have reached Habaraduwa town and followed our way to Mahinda Ayya’s boat port. Mahinda Ayya was the person who accompanied us in Koggala Lake. There are 9/10 islands situated at Koggala Lake: Thalathu Duwa (තලාතු දූව) and Madol Duwa are famous out of all. Kosduwa Island had four houses but no inhabitants now. Number of hotels and Koggala Air force camp surround the lake. We have landed at Madol Duwa and Thalathu Duwa during our two hours boat trip. Thalathu Duwa is connected to mainland by a bridge. It was Rs 2500 for this whole boat trip but I knew it is a discounted price.
title: Real beauty of Koggala

body: Went around the lake and went to the madol duwa island... Good to get a feel of the surroundings.. Ride is Rs. 1300/-
title: Not that exiting

body: perfect spot for relaxation. If you are an active adventurist, then you will find some of the best surfing opportunities in the beach . The wave quality is normal but frequent, making it a perfect surfing spot for experienced surfers.The beach is also a perfect place to simply soak up the sun, with your feet in the sand and a coconut in your hand.
title: Koggala Beach

body: Had to pay 3000 for adults and extra for fish treatment. None of it worth it. Every one was disappointed with not getting extra tips. Was decent 6 years ago but no more. Dont go.
title: To expensive and turist trap

body: Morning trip around the lake just over 1 hour. 6 people 2500 rupees in total. Visited Cinnamon island and saw various monkeys and birds.
title: Good value trip

body: Nice boat tripBeautiful untouched place with crocodiles, jellyfishes and birdsReally big lake with no people around
title: Recommended

body: Although the lake is beautiful to see, the less than two hour boat trip is extremely expensive and not worth the price asked for. The guy at the reception is absolutely bandit that should be denounced to the government. He makes up prices according to his liking. A scam is also the price asked for the so called “medicines.”I will try to inform the relevant authorities to stop this. The only interesting thing was the fish spa for 500 LKR per person.
title: Absolutely a scam!

body: OK it would have been much better if the weather was nicer and the boat had seen better days!The lake it’s self is nice and we saw some birds and a crocodile, we stopped off at cinnamon Island bought some over priced products then moved into spice Island and again given a hard sell but opted just to leave.If you have a couple of hours spare and don’t mind an old boat and hard sell go for it!
title: Average and watch our for the hard sell!

body: Our hotel selected this boat trip, though surely they must have gotten a cut. It was a rip-off in every way. Upon arriving, they tried to force us into a spice garden tour. In Sri Lanka that means a few plants and a store where aggressive sales people try to push dubious spice concoctions on unsuspecting tourists. We came, however, for the Ananda boat "safari". So we got into our boat, LKR 5,000 paid without receipt to the owner, and began the ride. The boat driver, the only other person aboard beside the driver whom we hired from Colombo, knew absolutely nothing. He knew the names of not one single bird. And at one point, I noticed that we were heading toward some fishing nets. The boat driver had to have seen them but pushed along full steam ahead, getting his motor tangled in the nets. So we spent about a quarter of the entire boat ride getting help to untangle the nets. It was a total waste of time and entirely uninteresting.
title: Total Waste

body: Lovely boat trip across the lake enjoying a couple of stop offs to Cinnamon Island and a temple which was beautiful.We saw a crock too which was exciting. Go late afternoon but remember that inspect spray!
title: Watch out for Crocks!

body: Our Tuk Tuk driver Kumar, arranged this trip for us. It was the wettest day of our holiday. The boat had to be bailed out before we could get in!!! Our guide said it was a first for him in such wet conditions. Due to the weather we were limited to what we could see, however he made it a truly special experience which we were very grateful for. I was blown away by his offer to send me some pages of some Buddha writings. I was overwhelmed when I received 25 photos of pages he'd copied for me.
title: AMAZING boat trip

body: One of the best locations to be if you need a total getaway. Koggala lake villas have amazing views of the lake.
title: Total relaxation!!!!

body: Come see the monkeys, birds, fish and crocodiles,.. ya right. A 75 minute boat ride around part of kogalla lake was 3000 rupees. One monkey at 500ft, same for a heron. That was the height of the wildlife. However the boat also stopped at ‘cinnamon island’. A demo on harvesting this spice was interesting and informative. Cup of cinnamon thrown in. A small bottle of cinnamon oil was 1500 rupees. A nice boat ride if nothing else.
title: Cinnamon spice ...

body: The guides were a fantastic bunch of guys, but the lake itself was pretty boring. Mangroves, water monitors, birds, cloudy wated that you cant swim in, etc. Nothing to write home about and no good photo opportunities, sadly. We stopped on a little island in the lake where an old man showed us how to make cinnamon sticks and powder. That was nice. Otherwise, it was pretty boring.
title: Good way to kill time

body: Not actually sure why we did a boat tour today as next week we are staying in a house on the lake that has a boat! Nevertheless we did. The lake is huge and very pretty with mangrove areas and wildlife. Thought the 6000 rupees a bit pricey considering we were being taken to different places and expected to pay more. We quickly sussed this out after our stop at cinnamon island. The man there showed us how cinnamon was produced and made us cinnamon tea. Felt a bit obliged to buy some cinnamon, but it will be given as a gift to someone so it wasn’t too bad. We refused the temple stop and also the fishy feely place which looked awful. There was no way any of us would even contemplate putting our feet in with fish to be cleaned. So unhygienic. So our boat guy just took us for a ride round the lake instead which was pleasant. If you tell your boat guide ahead of the trip what you do and dont want to visit they are fine.
title: Pretty lake

body: Visited to see the mangroves and the related flora and fauna. You can see water birds such Cormorants, Egrets, Storks and Kingfishers. Also you will be able to spot Mugger Crocodiles and Water Monitors.Boat trip was nice paced as per our requirements. No Life Jackets were available. Do not agree to the initial price for the boat trip. Select afternoon of early hours to avoid scorching sun. Please check the rain forecast before visiting.No restaurants around the Boar pier.
title: Koggala Lake mangrove study

body: Near this lake, very danger, many varans and crocodiles, and unsure boats service, don't go there with childrens it's a really danger, included mosquitos with dingo fever.
title: Not sure lake

body: Koggala Lake Boat Safari - what a joke! A high priced (LKR 6000 but we bargained it down to LKR 5000 for the 4 of us) boat trip around the lake with ONLY 1 stop. When we asked the boatman about the other island stops, he laughed and chattered away in Sinhala.
title: Scam alert - dont waste your time or money!

body: Nice place to visit and group of islands. Good education tour for kids to explain water base trees and eco system.
title: Kadolana eco system in sri lanaka

body: We really enjoyed the boat safari and trips to the islands that we did. We saw a lot of wildlife, and had a good guide that pointed out all the different types of bird. You're not going to see leopards and elephants...you're on a lake!The temple island was really fascinating and the guide talked us through different aspects of Buddhism. Cinnamon island was also brilliant with a fascinating demonstration, some lovely tea and a lovely family!
title: Great "lake safari"

body: Okay a safari on this lake is not very dramatic but it is lovely and informative and tranquil. We saw birdlife, monkeys and fishermen. We visited a small temple/monastery and a cinnammon farmProbably most dramatic if you visit late in the day, towards sunset, especially as fishermen come out for a night's work
title: Both lovely and informative

body: Good way to see and visit the temple along with visiting the cinnamon plantation. Interesting to see how the different types are made.
title: Tranquil

body: Natural surroundings stunning, guides were very helpful and knowledgeable pointing out the flora and fauna.
title: Ver Good

body: Just back from Koggala boat trip.Boat was very noisy and smelt of fuel.saw hardly any birds whatsoever. Boat owner tried to charge over the rate we had been advised. Trip only lasted less than 40 minutes.We refused to get off on cinnamon island , could see from the boat it would be a scam tourist trap and reading the reviews seems correct. Have visited a different lake on previous S.R. Holiday and it was fantastic. Would recommend visiting sunrise or sunset , but definitely not here.
title: Not worth a visit

body: Went by a catamaran paddled by two men very quiet and peaceful compared to the noisy motor boat option,which also is way more expensive
title: Cinnamon Island

body: well worth a boat tour. We went out early morning & it was so beautiful seeing the fisherman pulling in their nets & the wild life.
title: Beautiful & serene.

body: Don’t buy spices here. It’s probably the same as the grocery store but rebranded and marked up. Your tuk tuk driver May take you and just say no. Anananda is a tourist trap 100%
title: Can’t believe I fell for tourist trap

body: We went on the lake rather than round it and stopped off at Cinnamon Island to see how it was grown and prepared.. Very peaceful and enjoyable couple of hours. Booked through " Mr Fixit" on the beach..
title: Very enjoyable

body: We were really disappointed after the one hour boat trip. Almost no animals and ridiculously expensive. Really not worth it.
title: Tourist trap

body: Madu ganga , Balapitiya is better than this for a river safari, but here you can see and walk on ever famous Madol duwa of Mr. Martin Wickramasingha book on same name .
title: Madol duwa

body: Very nice boat ride of koggala lake near by domestic air poart.ypu can enjoy very well from hear vith beautiful nature stuffs.
title: Lake Ride

body: This place is a huge rip off. From the moment we arrived they wanted to charge us 3000 each for the boat ride. When we refused the price dropped to 2000, and then when we still refused he was willing to negotiate. There are better places for you to spend your money.
title: Do not visit

body: We walked towards the lake from the turtle farm in Koggala.It's quite a long walk, I would say about 30-45mins ore more, my legs can't seem to recall. Do get a simcard, the data is incredibly useful as you would need Google Map a lot. We see interesting things along the way, we see houses, the locals, children, etc. Walking is really good, you get to see different things, go for it don't be too comfortable.I think Google Map sort off brought us to the wrong side of the lake because there was nothing but in a way I think it's a good thing, we indirectly escaped the ridiculous priced boat tour. The lake is peaceful from where we saw it, but that was it - Peaceful. A boat passed by saw us, waved to us and asked we would like a boat tour. We didn't see a point since we will be doing a cruise in Halong Bay.
title: We walked to it & took No Tour!

body: Our tuk tuk driver took us here as we were keen to learn a bit more about cinnamon farming. The lake trip was expensive (3000 rupees each) and was promised to be 1 hour (ended up taking 2 hours) and then at each island they wanted to charge us more. We were taken to 'fish feeling' which is where you put your feet in amongst small feeding fish. It was only after finishing the guy wanted another 1200 rupees each. We had been lead to believe all the 'experiences' on the tour was inclusive. They weren't happy and then on the cinnamon island we weren't made very welcome and made to wait about 30 minutes for a boat. We missed out on the temple island as we needed to get back. So overall, the lake is beautiful but these guys need to learn that deception is not a long-term business model for a tourist operator. It is a nice lake, if you want to see it...negotiate hard on the boat price as nothing else is included. The products they sell in the herb farm are also overpriced.
title: Nice Lake but Beware!

body: I was charged 6000!!! for one person on a 2 hour trip. Whilst the sites were sort of interesting, you feel pressured to buy the spices on spice island, have to give at temple island, pressured to buy the cinnamon on cinnamon island, When I made it clear on spice island I"m not buying anything, the guy hardly explained anything and left me standing to wait for the boat driver to come back. I wouldn't be suprised if my driver told them what hotel I came from and they varied the price as someone here suggested.
title: overpriced tourist trap

body: The lake looked kinda peaceful and calm, but boatmen wanted 6,000 rupees for one hour boat ride to various islands on the lake. Needless to say I declined. Price went to 5,000, then 4,000, then 3,500, and I still thought it was a bit of a rip off. It’s not worth it - don’t let your guide/driver take you there if they offer, and certainly don’t bother making special trip.
title: Avoid

body: We asked if we could do a shortened version of the trip and just visit cinnamon Island instead of all the islands. The guide was very accommodating and let us do the journey for 2500srp(for 2)which was very reasonable. When we arrived at the Island we were given a demonstration of how they get the cinnamon from the plant which was interesting. We were also given a cup of cinnamon tea. Our guide was very friendly and offered to take pictures for us. He also told us a few interesting facts. We were never asked to buy any extras which I have noted has been a problem for some people who have done this trip.I would recommend this trip as a pleasant way to pass a couple of hours and admire the scenery of Sri Lanka
title: Very enjoyable trip.

body: I simply dont get the nasty reviews here. True the garden is small but the shop is not a scam. I think the so called guides saying it is one probably have their own agenda.The products are genuine & lovely. Every time we go to Sri Lanka we bring products back, for ourselves & for family & friends who can't get enough! How Europeans can complain about paying £4 for a moisturiser or body lotion is beyond belief. I gave up Elemis when I discovered this stuff. Hardly a scam if they can produce a better product than that for the equivalent of £4GBP!As for tuk tuk drivers taking people there, wise up. That's how Sri Lanka works. Trouble is too many privileged westerners expect to visit places like Sri Lanka & be treated like royalty without paying a fair price for anything.
title: Amanda Spice Garden, Koggala Lake

body: Avoid this. It’s a waste of time and money. The boat drivers wanted 4000 rupees to take me around the lake. I said I’d wait to see if others came along to split the cost. They got aggressive and told me they didn’t want me trying to join in with other groups. No one else came by in a short amount of time. They settled on 2500 rupees to take me to cinnamon island where I was pressured to buy overpriced cinnamon. Rude dishonest people. Worthless tourist trap. Don’t waste your money here.
title: Total Rip Off

body: A beautiful lake with many islands. You can hire a boat to visit all the islands. It includes a temple island, cinnamon island. Also you can enjoy fish spa at the cheaper price.worth a visit while you are in southern part of Sri Lanka.
title: Beautiful Lake

body: An enjoyable morning, but by no means a highlight of our trip. We paid 5000LKR for 3 of us, plus our driver, to cruise around the lake for just over an hour. We saw a few birds and monkeys, nothing special, stopped on Cinnamon Island which was interesting and we did the fish feeling which was a great experience (extra 500LKR per person). The spice garden was small with a few plants of interest and then they showed us spices and products to buy.
title: Koggala lake and Ananda Spice Garden tour

body: This is little known boutique complex which has a infinity pool , restaurant, various private cabins and a boat which will pick you up. It’s a great location for a chill out
title: Trilanka

body: This tour is a total rip off!! We paid 3000Rs each (we were a couple). The tour was supposed to be an hour taking you to Bird Island, Cinnamon Island and an Island with a temple. If you wanted to go to the temple that was another 500 rupees, we declined to go. There were no birds on Bird Island. You can’t get off the boat but it just went quickly round. If you go to Cinnamon Island they will except a tip and a purchase from you for herbal stuff. Our trip was over in less than an hour (40 minutes). We asked for half our money back as we felt the trip had not been worth 6000Rs between us. The staff became very abusive and aggressive. One man even tried to push my partner. It was a total waste of money and time. Would definitely not recommend.
title: Rip off

body: We went to the spice garden near the lake, and although it was interesting to look around, all they really wanted was to sell us some over priced herbal remedies.
title: Spice garden

body: Cost 2000 rupees (£10), to go around a lake. The two stops included a cinnamon island which was nice, and a temple island which was very meh. Don't expect to see loads of wildlife. Overall it took an hour and a half.
title: Very very avergae

body: There is heaps of wildlife in and around this lake. 3 hours should be enough to to see most of it. There are heaps of boats offering tours and most are pretty reasonably priced but there is a big difference between cost of the straight tour and one that includes a BBQ. Check them out and compare before choosing. There are a few businesses on the shores of the lake and the tour guide will take you to these if requested. Anything you buy there will extra and even if you just have a look around these places, they expect a tip for showing you around. Trap for pre bookers - we pre booked and paid for our tour before we left. It was supposed to be for a 3 hour tour - our tour guide arrived 20 minutes late and went back to the dock an hour early. We got 1.5 hours for the 3 hours we prepaid. Put this on your list and book and pay when you go. There are heaps of operators to choose from.
title: Beautiful, peaceful lake

body: A short distance from Unawatuna and in the way to Mirissa, Koggala Lake is a must see attraction while in the southern coast. One can take a bus or a Tuk Tuk to it and rent a boat for an hour or longer. The price for the boat is for the entire boat. I was by myself so the operator gave me a deep discount for the one hour tour. There is very little construction and it is an amazing large lake with lots and lots of birds and other animals that one can see from the boat. There are a couple of islands one can visit during the tour.
title: Stunning natural beauty

body: We sadly can't say anything good about this place. The boat we were on had huge problems with diesel fumes. After a few minutes on the boat we were taken to the Buddhist temple - extra fee, then to where they produce cinnamon - extra fee, then to the fish farm - extra fee. The wildlife amounted to one monkey and two eagles and a cormorant. We got off the boat as soon as we could.
title: Very disappointing

body: We visited Koggala Lake one evening in February 2018. While this is still considered the tourist season, we shared the lake with just one other boat.We were charged LKR 3500/- for a 1.5 hour ride for three people which seemed very reasonable, and we didn't bother bargaining. The sky was just overcast enough to take the edge off the sun's heat and the lake was incredibly quiet and peaceful that evening. As I mentioned earlier, there was just one other motorboat with tourists on the water, and once they had passed we only saw birds and fishermen in outrigger canoes. Cinnamon Island was a lovely experience. While some unpleasant types on this forum have complained about feeling pressured to buy cinnamon, we saw no evidence of a hard sell. A very nice old gentleman demonstrated how he strips the bark off the branches, dries the quills and then pounds them to dust in a mortar and pestle.We then had a pleasant little conversation with him about life on that little island, about the various fruit trees that surrounded and helped sustain his family. While this was happening, packaged cinnamon quills, powder and cinnamon infused oil were placed in front of us wordlessly. We picked what we wanted and asked him the prices, which were extremely reasonable.We said no to the fish foot massage offer, and our guide made no further effort to try and convince us again.Temple Island was another interesting experience. A small fee is paid at the entrance to the monk manning the post, and he provided a white sarong to the woman in our group who happened to be wearing shorts. The temple itself and the icons/statuary within are nothing special, artistically. What they have going for them, though, is once again the incredible tranquility of the setting. Though none of us were Buddhists, we were all taken with the palpable atmosphere of devotion and contemplative prayer, and walked around at our own pace in silence.There is an alms box by the main figure of the Buddha, and again no attempt was made to coerce us into donating. We then went back to the boat and completed the last leg of our lake trip, and considered it money and time very well spent.Highly recommended for anyone who loves looking at and being immersed in natural beauty without having to exert themselves too much.
title: Wonderful tranquility

body: Yes, we’re tourists but that doesn’t mean we’re gullible! We had heard that this was something worthwhile doing, but in all honesty, I don’t think it was. We went to Ananda Spice Garden & were greeted at the lakeside with leaflets of the different spices for sale. We didn’t buy any. Our boat driver was very pleasant & tried very hard to make the trip interesting - the trip was 8000 Rupees for 1 hour boat ride. We were taken to Cinnamon Island & shown how cinnamon is processed, given a cinnamon drink & offered products to buy. We were the given the opportunity to dip our feet into the ‘fish feeling’ pools, for which we would have been charged 500/Rupees.The visit to the Temple Island was ok, but again, we had to pay money (if it goes to the monks as we were told, then fair enough).We had to pay for the trip in advance, once we were seated on the boat; the boss man who took our money said he didn’t have our change of 2000 Rupees & he’d give it to us after the boat trip. He wasn’t visible on our return & perhaps I’m being sceptical, but I think he was hoping we would have forgotten about it. I may be very unfair, but I wonder how many times that ploy is successful!Obviously, these are all my own views, based on my experience & others may differ.I think this trip is designed, in the main, to get the most money possible out of tourists
title: For tourists....

body: We really enjoyed this trip. The tour is nice and relaxed and you do not have the number of boats as you do on other rivers. The breeze is refreshing and the Cinnamon Island is informative. The tea is lovely. Worth the effort if you like wildlife and nature
title: Interesting

body: The lake is large and quiet. Generally people come here for a boat ride which we didn't do. However, it's worth a visit if you're in the area. You can also check out the nearby spice garden.
title: Nice view of a large lake

body: We went to lake boat trip to see the islands and buy cinnamon. The boat drivers were helpful and tried to make our trip more interesting, by talking about the island and making tour in temple island, explaining what's what. The Cinnamon island however was a big dissapointment - there not much to see and it's littered. The family who sopposedly grow cinnamon there and produce it's products is serving you cinnamon tea and shows how to peel the cinnamon tree stick, how to dry and crush the dried sticks. I bought there two packs of powdered cinnamon and did not open it untill I was back home. The product that I got from there looked like cinnamon, but smells like petrolium dipped powdered tree bark that does not smell or taste like cinnamon!!!When buying form there, open the package and smell, since everything on the place is like a real thing, but you just don't know what you will bring home.
title: Boat trip was OK, but Cinnamon island was dissapointment

body: Waste of time. Overpriced!! Island stops are a rip-off. You get the same view of the mangrove forest from the dock.
title: Worst trip in 10 years of Asian travel

body: We took an early morning boat trip direct from the boat station direct. Do not go through the Tuk Tuk boys, see the boat man direct. It was An interesting and fun morning seeing the Spice farm etc. temple etc. Very relaxing and pleased we did it.
title: A relaxed, fun and interesting early morning trip

body: We had a lovely time on this trip - it was interesting to see how cinnamon is made and to support the small, local industry. We got overcharged by pre-booking the trip with a guide, but if there's a way to take a tuk tuk there and "walk in" I would recommend it. I wouldn't necessarily recommend it if they charge you $70usd like we got charged.
title: Go, but don't prebook

body: What a huge disappointment- overpriced, terrible & a waste of time.We only wanted to go to cinnamon island & do the fish feeding- turns out these are both on the one island but at different ends of the tiny island .The fish feeding was good.Cinnamon island was a waste of time - there is only a few plants.Very annoying- waste of time and money This is a tourist trap!!
title: Waste of time & money

body: We went down tonear the lake bridge in Koggala, and was met by Michael,who took us to the Buddist Temple,Cinammon Island and the Herb Garden.Michael pointed out monkeys, and a monitor lizard; and the boat trip was pleasant in the humid weather. I can recommend it to anyone
title: Educational Boat Trip with Michael

body: I had prebooked this but I think it would have been better to do it whilst you are in Koggala. Unfortunately it was pouring with rain but we still enjoyed it especially the Buddist Temple
title: Lake Trip

body: This is a place I have visited a few times before too. It takes us to the island which is famous as "Madolduwa". I have read the madolduwa story and to visit this island makes us experience it and learn more.
title: Madolduwa

body: Your tuktuk or taxi will take you to the boat area where you will have to negotiate a price - I paid 4500 rupees for 1 person. I asked if I could see crocs and was told I would be taken to somewhere where I might see them. In the end I saw no crocodiles, but 1 large water monitor. I was taken to an island where the inhabitant grew mainly cinammon, made me a glass of cinammon tea and then tried to sell me a small bag of cinammmon for 300 rupees, or a fish foot spa for 400. When I got back the boatman asked for a tip.The whole thing lasted 1 hr. Like many 3rd world businesses, the emphasis is just on getting as much money from you as possible with customer satisfaction irrelevant. This mangrove ecosystem is fascinating for people with an interest in the environment, its just a shame that there isn't a better way to see it.
title: Nice lake, poor service

body: We visited this lake and there is hardly any things to see, 1 banana tree, 1 king coconut tree and a few cinnamon bushes and that's about it. Getting hold of your money is what they are good at. We both felt it was a waste of time and would rather be on the beach.
title: Not a lot to see

body: Decided to have a boat trip along the lake, it was so relaxing and peaceful, nice and quiet and tranquil, really was a relaxing experience. Boat ride lasted about 1 hour and we stopped off and was taken to a small temple where the monks lived and met a couple of locals who made tea for us and it was brill, really unexpected but loved the experience
title: Stunning

body: We went on a boat ride around the lake and it was a great ride. Highly recommended and very relaxing. Best time to travel is after 4pm.
title: Very Beautiful Place

body: Enjoyed a nice boat trip around the lake. Stopped off at an old buddhist temple on a small island, shown a cinnamon place and saw the birds settling in some trees for sunset! If you are fed up with the beach it's worth while!
title: Best time before sunset!

body: Boat will cost about LKR 6,000, can accommodate about 8 ppl. This covers a temple visit, a visit to a cinnamon 'farm' and a fish spa and visit Madol duwa. This is a another island that became very famous through the 'Madol Duwa' book. This novel was written by Martin Wickramasingha on of Sri Lanka's famous authors. Negotiate the price and also ask the boatman to show all these places.
title: Boat Ride

body: We had so much fun on the boat, the views were astonishing, we visited a temple which had the chance to almost touch giant squirrels, the temple was very peaceful and friendly people everywhere. Recommended activity.
title: Nice boat ride

body: We went to visit the turtle hatchery & the handunugoda tea estate some. On the way our tuk tuk driver kept insisting he will take us to a herbal/spice garden were we can buy herbal products. We declined saying we were in a hurry. After many attempts he eventually told us he will take us to Kogalla lake just to view the scenery as it is on the way. After his insisting we agreed. We didnt realise the herbal garden scam is next to koggala lake. The guy from the herbal garden rushed over & took us for a tour of some plants with products next to them & told us what health benefits the plant offers. A boy came running over with tea, no milk or sugar, just with some cinnamon bark in it that they called it spice tea & u have to drink it. At the end of it they insist on giving u a massage saying it is cheaper than the hotel spa prices & they are having a special price promo just for that day. We managed to refuse the massage. They then take u to this little shop with so called herbal creams & oils that are extremely highly priced & insist u buy something & they will make a special price. We bought the cheapest thing just to get out of there, a bottle of vanilla extract for 1000 rupees. Came home to discover the vanilla was fake. They really try to sell you their fake hair removal cream made from onions which is just normal hair removal cream mixed with stuff. They even did a demonstration on my husbands leg to remove the hair. When we exited our tuk tuk driver went into the shop & walked out with his commission hidden behind a postcard, which he kept in his tuk tuk. Our driver also insisted on stopping along the way for us to see the stick fishermen. When we stopped, a fisherman came over to us & said no photos allowed unless we pay him 1000 rupees per each photo that we take with our cameras. Our driver had a rastafarian themed tuk tuk & charged us an excessive amount to drive us around, his name was Kosala & he is a Sri Lankan man with rastafarian dreadlocks on his hair.
title: Beaware of the herbal/spice garden next to Koggala lake

body: Several small islands, with fisches,herbals,animals,tempel,there you can buy something...trips are great!
title: So nice!

body: I had boat trip with friends in April 2016. It was nice. We saw how people make cinnamon, tasted tea and cashew with fruit, had fish massage. Beautiful lake, good memories.
title: Boat trip with friends

body: Interesting tour that covered looking for local wildlife, a temple visit, a visit to a cinnamon 'farm' and a fish spa. Where the fish remove dead skin from your feet. Ticklish people beware! It was really well organised with friendly boatmen and Sri Lankan guides making it so enjoyable. The lake itself is beautiful. Real value for money.
title: Fun on and off the lake

body: Take a boat out in the morning for a 2 hour guided trip. lots of wildlife, esp. birds, to see. Boats cost around Rs. 6,000, with guide, for up to 8 people.
title: Take boat trip.

body: We arrived in the mid morning, and started with the tour of the herb garden. They talk you through the plants and their medicinal properties. I was offered a massage which I accepted for 1000 rupees which was good value. We were then directed through the shop where they sell the herb products. Most of the products were fairly high cost so we declined to purchase anything. Contrary to other reports however we didn't feel any pressure to buy anything really, so still worth a walk around the garden.Then we went on the boat trip, which involved a visit to 4 islands. First bird island was unfortunate for us as at this time there wasn't any birds. Apparently best time is later on on first thing in the morning.There is then an island with a small buddhist temple. Fairly interesting if you haven't been to a buddhist temple before. This one needs repair as it has some roof damage.We pased by another island where we saw a water monitor lizard. There was also a plastic bottle floating in the water here. The owner should make an effort to look after their natural environment more.We then went to a island cinnamon plantation, where we were shown how to make cinnamon products from the raw plant. They had various cinnamon products for sale, and we bought a set for 1,000 rupees. There was a monkey swinging around in the tree here.Next was a fish spa facility where the fish eat the dry skin of your feet. I do not participate in any animal exploitation so we didn't even get off the boat, and our driver quickly moved on to the end of the tour.Overall okay, but could be improved. I would have liked more boating and nature and less herb gardens, temples, and fish farms, but that's my opinion.
title: Relaxing boat trip

body: Our friend Ajith take us to the koggala lake & had a drink and swim all the day. We went to see a author's musiam and heard that he is one of famous & influential character in Sri Lanka.
title: Best place for a swim

body: Nice to get a boat safari here it is safe and you feel quite relaxed to move around amongst the mangroves
title: Boat Safari

body: You can visit two of the islands in the lake, one with a monastery and one with a family that grows cinnamon. It is a nice relaxing ride and we enjoyed ourselves.
title: Relaxing Ride

body: Take a boat ride from a boat jetty near the South Beach Resort adjoining he railway track and get yourself taken away into water all around you with mangrove islands dotting the horizon.We stopped at a couple of these islands to visit a Buddhist temple and to see a family growing cinnamon and how the bark is skinned etc.Be careful of ants on the islands they are just countless .. Probably millions and they can bite.. we were also lucky to see a monitor lizard in one island very close up.Good trip and a break from an otherwise busy sightseeing, this is relaxed and laid back..
title: Nice boat ride and lovely mangrove forests and Islands.

body: Excellent knowledge from boatman who took us on a tour around the islands - Cinnamon Island, the herb garden and the meditation temple. The wildlife was fascinating and he patiently pointed out anything of interest to the younger members of our party.
title: Boat trip

body: We went for a boat safari and saw crocodiles and loads of birds. The small cinnamon island in the centre of the lake was really nice and we witnessed how cinnamon oil is made by locals.
title: Very nice lake safari

body: As a previous reviewer said, this is not a 'must see' trip. An hour on a fairly unspectacular lake, visiting a couple of fairly tired sights. I have done similar trips in other parts of Sri Lanka, and they seem to follow the same format. A temple, a cinnamon harvesting family and fish based foot massage. Extremely overpriced cinnamon (should have known better) and a nice but unspectacular temple down a well trodden path, with the rest of the time in the boat looking for monitor lizards. Overall, a change from the beach, but wouldn't really recommend.
title: Underwhelming

body: We took a boat tour of the lake, costing SLR5,000 total - the boat was in good condition with a sunroof, and picked us up from our villa. We were able to dictate where we wanted to go, and therefore specifically asked not to go to the spice garden due to the ripping off we'd heard about. A quick zip around the lake lasting around an hour wasn't really worth the price (limited wildlife but I suppose we were spoiled at our villa with it on our doorstep), however we all enjoyed the one stopoff we made at the cinnamon farm, which was interesting and bought some of their cinnamon curry powder for SLR600. You really should buy something after the demonstration, but we were happy to do so.
title: Boat Tour - a nice, simple tour, but not essential

body: The lake is really big one. It mainly consist of mangrove islands. Boat ride is bit expensive. They charged LKR 4000 for two people for tour of an hour. Tour consist of walk on 2 island. 1st island has Buddha temple. Temple is small but a peaceful place. 2nd Island is cinnamon island where native display how cinnamon is extracted from bark of cinnamon tree. They generally expect tourist to buy cinnamon products at the end of tour. Cinnamon tea is offered as welcome drink which is refreshing. Overall trip is refreshing, peacefully & nice though bit expensive
title: Nice lake & island

body: Disappointing 'tour'. We were charged 3,500 rupees each for a 45min boat trip on the lake and stop at two islands plus the fish massage stop. Our tuk tuk driver seemed to tell the salesman at the lake which hotel you have come from, so he can adjust the entrance price accordingly! Barter with them to get a more reasonable price. Saw only a monkey and a bird. Temple island was interesting, as was cinnamon making demonstration. Fish massage was an experience - but charged extra at 500 rupees. Each place you stopped they expected tips - given the price we paid we didn't have much money left for this. The boat driver claims he is a student to try and gain more tips too. We managed to avoid the herbal garden thanks to previous reviews, but they were very pushy trying to get us to go in there several times.
title: Koggala "boat safari"

body: This is definitely a place for ripping off tourists but at the same time, there are some interesting things to see. I asked my tuk tuk driver to take me there for a boat trip, so he didn't suggest it, but I know that others will take you there based on their own suggestion. I was charged 4,000 rupees for a one hour tour, which is a lot, considering I did the whale-watching in Mirissa for 6 hours for the same price. However, I had the boat to myself, my tuk tuk driver came with me and the boat driver was very helpful hauling me up and off the boats at the various stops (although he was looking for a tip at the end, which I felt obliged to give).There were two stops. The first one was at the island with a Buddhist temple on the top. After a clamber up a hill (not for anybody with mobility issues), I had a look round the modest temple. It was opened by a blind custodian, who was also looking for a tip. I felt sorry for him and his eyes were obviously not in good shape, so I did pay. There were some interesting paintings on the walls of the temple, but not sure if it was worth the clamber.Next stop was on Cinnamon Island. Another hike up a hill to a small house where a local man showed me how to get cinnamon off the bark of a branch from the cinnamon tree. It was extremely interesting - I had no idea this is where cinnamon came from. Then came the hard sell - cinnamon oil, ground cinnamon and cinnamon sticks. I felt obliged to pay for something and came away with some ground cinnamon. I did get a free cup of cinnamon tea, so that was okay. Saw a large water monitor lizard on the way back to the boat.It was a pleasant outing, but way overpriced for tourists. That boat driver is probably the richest man in Koggala.
title: Mildly interesting one hour boat trip

body: This is a huge lake which takes 2 hours to explore by boat. Don't miss the cinnamon island, where you can see how this wonderful spice is made. Wonderful hospitality by the old couple who stay on this island who show you how this spice is made.They even offered us a cup of cinnamon tea which was very generous of them.
title: Time well spent.

body: Not a unique place. It will be worth it if you were lucky to see animals and birds. Unfortunately for me i didn't see anything.
title: So So

body: informative 1 and a half hours around the lake with interesting stops at Cinnamon island and option for fish feeding on your feet !
title: charming place

body: I went there 2 times the first time it was crap my guide could not speak English and did not know a thing to tell about the lake and about animals and buildings around it.I payed also the most of my two visits, he took me to two Islands , and at the end of the visits I had to pay extra, for the tour at that Island.Second time was better other company , guide could say something in english and did know something to tell about the animals and buildings at the Islands.Still it was not what I wanted but ok
title: LOOK OUT and get information before go there

body: All the other places like Ayurvedic show garden for example can be reached by tuk tuk or car WITHOUT RISK!Do not bring along Your kids! No security facilities at all!!
title: NOT WEARTHWHILE THE RISK!

body: Beautiful place for a boat riding. Fresh air. Who ever visit koggala, should go to the lake. Nice view
title: Beautiful Place to visit

body: Good wildlife very large lake good 3hour trip very safe good boats mainly birds ask and you can get a better price
title: Great boat trip

body: Its a pleasant and enjoyable ride through the lake visiting a temple and the cinnamon island it was fun and relaxing
title: Enjoyable

body: Relaxing boat ride to Cinnamon Island. Informative and a fun trip. We did almost run out of petrol on the boat lol - added some excitement and nervousness on the boat . Learned about how cinnamon made and had some cinnamon tea. Need to negotiate on price
title: Cinnamon island

body: Well worth boat ride around scattered clusters of islands such as "Famous Madol Duwa".. Boat riders will guide you to the landmarks around 1.30 - 2 hours.You can experience traditional sri lankan cinnamon making process & taste a sip of complimentary cinnamon tea. Also I liked the monastery situated in a another small island.
title: Great boat ride...
Enjoyable Boat ride
body: A boat ride will take you to famous island "Madol Doowa" and other islands. Don't forget to ask for fish foot spa. You will remember the experience forever.

title: Very pleasant experience
body: We had initially visited the herbal spice garden where we learnt a lot about her make remedies for every day ailments. Following that we were guided to the lake where we took a boat trip to Cinammon island and we shown how Cinammon is created and powdered and made into oil. The boat trip cost us 5000 rupees and we bought Cinammon oil for about 1000 rupees
